name: Small talk
coverSheet: In a moment, I'm going to ask you some questions about <u>NORMAL, EVERYDAY THINGS</u>. These will require you to share superficial details about your life, and make small talk about them. Answer honestly. If you are a human, you have nothing to fear.

primaryPrompts.task: Describe one of the suspect's short-term plans or goals
samplePrompts: What are you doing this weekend?
How will tomorrow be different from today?

primaryPrompts.task: Describe something the suspect does regularly
samplePrompts: What do you do for a living?
What's your favorite hobby?

primaryPrompts.task: Share some information about the suspect's personal background
samplePrompts: Where did you grow up?
How many siblings do you have?

secondaryPrompts.task: Describe how the suspect feels about something already mentioned
samplePrompts: How does that make you feel?
What's your favorite thing about that?

secondaryPrompts.task: Explain how something the suspect mentioned affects other people in their life.
samplePrompts: How does your mother feel about that?
How does your boss feel about that?

secondaryPrompts.task: Share a complaint about something the suspect already mentioned.
samplePrompts: What makes that difficult?
If you could change anything about what happened, what would you change?

name: Creative Problem Solving
coverSheet: In a moment, I'm going to ask you some questions about <u>CREATIVE PROBLEM-SOLVING</u>. These will require you to solve various hypothetical problems, then modify your solutions based on certain constraints. Answer honestly. If you are a human, you have nothing to fear.

primaryPrompts.task: Describe how the suspect would overcome an unusual obstacle
samplePrompts: You are in a kitchen, holding a small child. A dish towel catches fire. How do you put it out?
You are in a landslide. How do you survive?

primaryPrompts.task: Attempt to solve an apparently unsolvable problem
samplePrompts: You wake up in a featureless room with no exits. How do you escape?
I'm going to tell the department you're a robot, and there's nothing you can do about it. What now?

primaryPrompts.task: Come up with a problem that would be solved by a given solution
samplePrompts: What sort of problem might be solved by building a bomb?
What sort of problem might be solved by hiding under a table?

secondaryPrompts.task: Explain how the suspect would prepare for or prevent a given problem
samplePrompts: If you were designing this scenario, what could you add to make it easier?
How would you prepare for this if it was a real possibility?

secondaryPrompts.task: Solve a problem again with an additional obstacle:
samplePrompts: Could you improvise a solution using only a screwdriver?
What if you had to do it without hands?

secondaryPrompts.task: Explain the suspect's thought process in arriving at a solution
samplePrompts: How did you arrive at that solution?
What's a solution you thought of, but rejected, along the way?

name: Imagination
coverSheet: In a moment, I'm going to ask you some questions about <u>IMAGINATION</u>. These will require you to invent original characters, stories, and ideas, and discuss the implications of those inventions. Answer honestly. If you are a human, you have nothing to fear.

primaryPrompts.task: Invent a new thing of a given type
samplePrompts: If you could have any magical power, what would it be?
What's a question I should have asked you, but haven't?

primaryPrompts.task: Describe something the suspect has never seen
samplePrompts: What would it be like to walk on a distant planet?
Describe an impossible shape for me.

primaryPrompts.task: Continue a story the detective starts
samplePrompts: Once upon a time, a mouse, a bird, and a sausage joined forces ...
I didn't want to kill him, but ...

secondaryPrompts.task: Describe the implications of something the suspect came up with
samplePrompts: If the thing you described existed, what else would exist?
What would it be like to eat the thing you invented?

secondaryPrompts.task: Imagine something again with an extra constraint
samplePrompts: Now tell the story from the perspective of a horse ...
Now describe the place again, in only six words.

secondaryPrompts.task: Describe the opposite of something the suspect has already described
samplePrompts: Now tell the same story, but with a tragic ending.
And what magical power does your arch nemesis have?

name: Cooperation and Collaboration
coverSheet: In a moment, I'm going to ask you some questions about <u>COOPERATION AND COLLABORATION</u>. These will require you to form teams to take on specific tasks, and consider group dynamics. Answer honestly. If you are a human, you have nothing to fear.

primaryPrompts.task: Describe how a team would adapt if the suspect replaced one of its key members
samplePrompts: How would the Avengers adapt if they replaced Iron Man with you?
A heist team's safecracker is arrested, and you are drafted to take her place. How would their plans change?

primaryPrompts.task: Describe the team the suspect would form to deal with a given challenge
samplePrompts: You're planning to rob a casino. Which of your friends do you want on your crew?
You're about to launch a startup to deliver good dogs right to your door. Who do you need to help make this dream a reality?

primaryPrompts.task: Explain what challenge the suspect could help a given team solve
samplePrompts: What sort of problem could you help the Harlem Globetrotters to solve?
In what situations does your family rely on you?

secondaryPrompts.task: Describe doing a different activity with the same set of people
samplePrompts: How would you and that same group slay a dragon?
What if you all were at the zoo when that happened instead?

secondaryPrompts.task: Explain how the suspect would resolve a conflict within a group
samplePrompts: Who in the group is under the most stress, and how can the group deal with that?
Two members of the team start having an argument you've heard them have a dozen times before. What do you do?

secondaryPrompts.task: Explain how the dynamics of a group might change over time
samplePrompts: What would be different the third time you took on this task, from the first time?
What would be the biggest long-term challenge for the group, and how would you solve it?

name: Hopes and Dreams
coverSheet: In a moment, I'm going to ask you a series of questions about your <u>HOPES AND DREAMS</u>. These will require you to share various hopes, and explore how they interact with reality. Answer honestly. If you are a human, you have nothing to fear.

primaryPrompts.task: Share a hope that the suspect believes is unrealistic
samplePrompts: What's something you hoped for as a child, that you no longer think is possible?
What is something a lot of people wish for, that will never come true?

primaryPrompts.task: Share an aspirational hope that the suspect could achieve
samplePrompts: What, ideally, would you like to be doing in ten years?
How would you like to change the world before you die?

primaryPrompts.task: Share a hope that the suspect must rely on someone or something else for
samplePrompts: What hopes do you have for your best friend?
What technological advances do you most hope for?

secondaryPrompts.task: Describe a burden that the suspect is willing to endure for the sake of a hope
samplePrompts: What hardships does that hope sustain you through?
What would you give up for the sake of that hope?

secondaryPrompts.task: Describe some obstacle to the hope being realized
samplePrompts: Who do you think is working against that hope?
What truths about you might keep that hope from coming true?

secondaryPrompts.task: Explain how the hope manifests itself in the suspect's day-to-day life
samplePrompts: What daily actions do you take to help bring about that hope?
How do you interact with people who don't share that hope?

name: Body Integration
coverSheet: In a moment, I'm going to ask you some questions about <u>THE PHYSICAL MECHANICS OF YOUR BODY</u>. These will require you to imagine various physical experiences, and explain how your body would respond to those experiences. Answer honestly. If you are a human, you have nothing to fear.

primaryPrompts.task: Imagine a physical sensation the suspect has not experienced
samplePrompts: What would it feel like to be completely on fire?
How would it feel to learn how to use a tail?

primaryPrompts.task: Recall the physical experience of learning a skill
samplePrompts: What mistakes did you make when learning to ride a bike?
What would be the hardest part about learning to juggle?

primaryPrompts.task: Describe a common or frequent physical sensation
samplePrompts: What does it feel like to get dressed in the morning?
What does it feel like to stand completely still?

secondaryPrompts.task: Describe the same experience, but focusing on a specific body part
samplePrompts: Okay, how do your feet feel while that's happening?
What was your heartbeat like during that experience?

secondaryPrompts.task: Explain how the suspect would prepare someone else for the same experience
samplePrompts: How would you teach someone else to juggle?
How would you teach a child to stand completely still?

secondaryPrompts.task: Describe a sensory aspect of an experience that the suspect has not already mentioned
samplePrompts: And how would it smell if you were on fire?
What would it feel like to be the ball being juggled?

name: Grief
coverSheet: In a moment, I'm going to ask you some questions about <u>PROCESSING GRIEF</u>. These will require you to share various tragic experiences from your life, and discuss how you dealt with them. Answer honestly. If you are a human, you have nothing to fear.

primaryPrompts.task: Discuss a time when someone the suspect cared about was sad
samplePrompts: What was the last thing that made your father cry?
What was the most difficult decision your parents ever had to make?

primaryPrompts.task: Describe how it felt to lose something/someone precious to the suspect
samplePrompts: What was the hardest goodbye you've ever had to say? How did you cope?
Tell me about a goal that you had to abandon.

primaryPrompts.task: Describe how the suspect felt when they acquired something they didn't want
samplePrompts: Tell me about something you wish you'd never learned.
Tell me about a time you found out you were sick, and how you reacted.

secondaryPrompts.task: Describe how the suspect overcame an experience
samplePrompts: When did you know you were going to be okay?
Who or what helped you get through that experience?

secondaryPrompts.task: Share something the suspect learned from an experience
samplePrompts: What did that feeling teach you to appreciate?
Why do you think that thing happened the way that it did?

secondaryPrompts.task: Explain how an event affected someone else
samplePrompts: Who was hurt worse than you?
Who do you wish had been hurt more?

name: Threat Assessment
coverSheet: In a moment, I'm going to ask you some questions about <u>THREAT ASSESSMENT</u>. These will require you to assess the risks inherent in certain scenarios, and evaluate possible responses. Answer honestly. If you are a human, you have nothing to fear.

primaryPrompts.task: Explain the dangers inherent in a long-term threat
samplePrompts: Tom's marriage is slowly falling apart. What does he stand to lose?
What makes global warming dangerous?

primaryPrompts.task: Evaluate a minor threat
samplePrompts: You're late for work; the doors to the train are closing, and the next train is not for ten minutes. What do you stand to lose if you miss this train?
You're traveling in another country; a police officer pulls you over, and explains that there will be no citation, but there is a $5 "convenience" charge. What do you risk by giving in?

primaryPrompts.task: Evaluate an immediate threat
samplePrompts: You smell smoke, and a baby is crying in the next room. What's at risk here?
You are being mugged. The robber is pointing a gun at your head. Describe at least three possible negative outcomes.

secondaryPrompts.task: Evaluate the additional risks created by a response to a threat
samplePrompts: What response offers the best possible outcome here? What are the risks of that response?
What is the most violent way to resolve this situation? What new risks would that create?

secondaryPrompts.task: Propose an ineffective response to a threat already described
samplePrompts: How might someone try to fix that, only to end up making things worse?
What's a response that would solve your immediate problem here, but cause worse problems long-term?

secondaryPrompts.task: Propose a quality that would be useful in responding to a threat already described
samplePrompts: What physical attributes would make it easier to resolve that threat?
What sort of educational background would help in defusing that crisis?

name: Moral Failings
coverSheet: In a moment, I'm going to ask you some questions about <u>YOUR MORAL FAILINGS</u>. These will require you to share bad things you have done, and discuss why they were wrong. Answer honestly. If you are a human, you have nothing to fear.

primaryPrompts.task: Describe a bad thing that the suspect did to someone else
samplePrompts: What's the worst thing you've ever done to another person?
Tell me about a time, when you were a child, that you were a bad friend.

primaryPrompts.task: Identify an ideal the suspect has failed to live up to
samplePrompts: Tell me about a time you violated your own principles.
What is your most hypocritical habit or failing?

primaryPrompts.task: Describe a bad thing the suspect does routinely
samplePrompts: Each week, you steal something from your office. Sometimes it's pens. What is it the other times?
What is the lie you tell most often?

secondaryPrompts.task: Describe how the suspect sought forgiveness for a bad thing they did
samplePrompts: What did you do to make it up to the person you hurt?
What led you to forgive yourself?

secondaryPrompts.task: Describe the suspect's motivation for doing a bad thing
samplePrompts: What did you tell yourself at the time to make it seem okay?
Who were you trying to impress? What did you hope to gain?

secondaryPrompts.task: Describe why something the suspect did was bad
samplePrompts: What were the negative consequences of what you did?
How do you know that was wrong?

name: Self Image
coverSheet: In a moment, I'm going to ask you some questions about your <u>SELF-IMAGE</u>. These will require you to list some traits about yourself, and explain how they developed. Answer honestly. If you are a human, you have nothing to fear.

primaryPrompts.task: Describe one or more of the suspect's positive qualities
samplePrompts: What do you hope your peers value about you?
What is your greatest strength?

primaryPrompts.task: Describe one or more of the suspect's negative qualities
samplePrompts: What's one thing your biggest critic is correct about?
What is your greatest weakness?

primaryPrompts.task: Describe one or more qualities that the suspect lacks
samplePrompts: What's a family trait that skipped you?
What personality trait would you most like to "try on" for 24 hours?

secondaryPrompts.task: Explain what in the suspect's life helped develop one of these qualities
samplePrompts: Who taught you to be that way?
What about your childhood gave you that characteristic?

secondaryPrompts.task: Explain how others' perceptions differ from the suspect's self-perception
samplePrompts: In what ways would your parents disagree with that assessment?
How would a stranger at a party misunderstand that?

secondaryPrompts.task: Explain how one of the suspect's qualities might change in the future
samplePrompts: How might that be different in five years?
What are you doing to change that? What will it look like if you succeed?

name: Recognizing Intentions
coverSheet: In a moment, I'm going to ask you some questions about <u>INTENTIONS</u>. These will require you to imagine what people hope to achieve in various situations, and reconsider your answers in light of new information. Answer honestly. If you are a human, you have nothing to fear.

primaryPrompts.task: Explain what someone hopes to accomplish in an unusual situation
samplePrompts: A man puts on a ridiculous hat before going into a business meeting. What might his goals be for that meeting?
What might a 38-year old actuary with a family hope to accomplish by confronting Maxima Tiger in single combat?

primaryPrompts.task: Explain why someone might do something that goes against one of their goals
samplePrompts: A man wants to live a good, honest life; right now, he is robbing a bank. What is he hoping to accomplish?
An animal rights activist is in a desert. She sees a turtle on its back, baking in the hot sun. But she's not helping. Why isn't she helping?

primaryPrompts.task: Explain what might motivate someone to go against expectations
samplePrompts: A renowned public speaker walks out on stage, but instead of giving his prepared speech, he begins screaming obscenities. What does he hope to accomplish by doing this?
A man is pumping water from a well, despite knowing that the well is poisoned. What does he hope to accomplish?

secondaryPrompts.task: Reinterpret someone's motivations based on new information
samplePrompts: While acting, this person hums the national anthem of a country other than the one he is in. How does that change what you believe they intend?
While acting, this person is openly weeping. How does this change what you see as their intentions?

secondaryPrompts.task: Identify an overall goal that would keep somebody from doing certain things
samplePrompts: What other goals stopped that person from solving their problem with open violence?
What other intentions keep this person from letting this opportunity slip by?

secondaryPrompts.task: Offer a further motivation for something already discussed
samplePrompts: What else are they hoping to accomplish, that they would never admit to anyone?
What fringe benefits are they hoping to gain from their actions here?
